questions: The specification says 'Sort coordinates initially by rows in ascending order. Also, sort coordinates in descending order.' This is contradictory. Does it mean sort by rows ascending, then within each row sort columns descending (as the reference solution does), or sort by rows ascending, then sort the entire list again by columns descending (which would intermix rows)?
Should the function find all occurrences of integer x, or only the first occurrence per row?
If x appears multiple times in the same row, should the column indices be sorted in descending order as stated, or should they be returned in the order they are encountered (left-to-right)?

Is the input guaranteed to contain only integers, or could there be other types? If other types exist, should we compare x to them using equality (==) which might work for some types, or strictly require type int?
Should the function handle nested lists that are deeper than 2 dimensions? If so, how should coordinates be represented?
What should be returned if lst is None instead of a list?
If a row is empty, should it be skipped entirely, or should we still consider it (and find no matches)?
Is the coordinate tuple (row, column) where column is the index within the row, or the position from the start of the entire flattened structure?
